newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila extends ceasefire in troubled Mindanao.
newsitem.headline: Manila extends ceasefire in troubled Mindanao.

text.p: The Philippine armed forces on Thursday extended a ceasefire on Mindanao island after former Moslem guerrilla chief Nur Misuari visited a rebel base to ask his former comrades to resume peace talks.

A unilateral military ceasefire that was to end on Friday has been extended by four days to pave the way for the resumption of talks with the insurgent Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), the military said.
The government and the MILF were to discuss a general ceasefire in Mindanao and prepare the agenda for formal talks on ending the southern conflict.
The MILF cancelled talks last month after clashes that ended with the capture by government forces of a MILF base in Maguindanao province.
Misuari visited the MILF's main Camp Abubakar in Maguindanao on Wednesday as special envoy of President Fidel Ramos and talked with MILF military vice chairman Al Haj Murad.

Misuari heads the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), the largest guerrilla group in Mindanao until he signed a peace deal with Manila last September. He is now governor of a semi-autonomous Moslem area.
MILF, with an estimated 8,000 fighters, is a breakaway guerrilla faction still fighting for an Islamic state.

Murad told Misuari he would reopen talks if government forces stopped their offensive and withdrew from the MILF camp seized in last month's fighting, MILF vice chairman for political affairs, Ghazali Jaafar, told Reuters.
"Brother Nur said he will bring this to the president and he promised to help," Jaafar said.
The military said over 70 guerrillas and 15 soldiers died in fighting last month. Jaafar said the MILF lost 20 dead.
